data.name: Valérien
data.gender_notes: Valérien is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Latin, Valérien means 'strength' or 'health' derived from the Roman god Valerius. The name was given to infants for protection, vitality, and robust health. The name Valérien carries the meaning “Strength, health, and vigor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Valérien usually hope their child will grow to embody strength, health, and vigor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of resilience and endurance.
data.etymology: Valérien belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strength, health, and vigor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Valérien total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: ולריאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ולריאן (Valéryan) היא שם נשים המשמר בערכו הקדום של שם העברי שאל, שפירושו 'בן-אלי' או 'בעל כוח'. השם נמצא בקשר עם הצורה היוונית Βαλεριανός (Valerianos) והלטינית Valerianus, שפירושם 'בעל-חזקה' או 'בעל כוח'. השם Valérien הוא שם נשים נדיר, שפירושו 'בעל-כוח ובן-אלי'.

in_greek.name: Βαλεριανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Βαλεριανός (Valerianós) הεί שάνθος που συνδέεται με την αρχαία ελληνική λέξη Βαλεριανός, η οποία σημαίνει 'αυτός με τη δύναμη' ή 'αυτός με την ηρωϊκή δύναμη'. Ο Βαλεριανός είναι ένα σπάνιο όνομα που συνδέεται με την κλασική ελληνική και ρωμαϊκή κουλτούρα, και έχει συνδεθεί με την ιδέα της δύναμης και της ηρωϊκότητας.

in_latin.name: Valerianus
in_latin.long_meaning: Valerianus est nomen masculinum quod significat 'homo potentia' seu 'homo virtus'. Nomen hoc a Valeria, nomine feminino, ortum est, quae significat 'fortis' seu 'fortitudo'. Valerianus est nomen rarum quod est in usu in Ecclesia Christiana ab antiquitate.

in_english.name: Valérien
in_english.meaning: bearing strength and son of Eli
in_english.long_meaning: Valérien is a rare given name that has its roots in the ancient Hebrew name Sha'al, meaning 'son of Eli' or 'bearing strength'. The name is connected to the Greek form Βαλεριανός (Valerianós) and the Latin form Valerianus, meaning 'bearing strength' or 'man of power'. Valérien is a unisex name that conveys strength, courage, and faith. In Christian tradition, the name Valérien is associated with the virtues of courage and perseverance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Valérien has its roots in ancient Roman culture. It was a popular name among the noble Roman families, signifying strength and vitality. In the Christian context, it was given to infants to protect them from harm and instil a sense of robustness and vitality.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Valérien holds a deep spiritual significance. It symbolizes the inner strength that a Christian derives from their faith. It is a reminder that as believers, we are not alone in our struggles and that God is our source of strength. The name also reflect the physical and spiritual health that comes from living a God-centered life and seeking His guidance and wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Valérien is a name of Roman origin, meaning "strong, healthy, or vigorous." In the Christian context, it symbolizes the strength and vitality of one's faith and commitment to God. The name may also signify a person who, like St. Valerian, is a protector and defender of Christianity in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference: Valérien I, also known as Valerian, was a Roman Emperor from AD 253 to 260. He was born in the province of Pannonia and was a member of the military caste. Valerian is best known for his military campaigns against the Sassanian Empire, during which he was captured and held for ransom. This event marked the first time a Roman Emperor had been captured in battle and it greatly weakened the Roman Empire.
historical_references.context: Roman Empire, Military Campaigns against the Sassanian Empire

historical_references.reference: Valérien II, also known as Flavius Valerianus, was a Western Roman Emperor from 365 to 367. He was the son of Valentinian I and was appointed as emperor by his father during his deathbed scene. Valerian II is best known for his inability to prevent the Visigoths, led by Fritigern, from sacking Rome in 367. This event marked the first time Rome had been sacked since the sack of Alaric I in 410 BC and it greatly weakened the Western Roman Empire.
historical_references.context: Western Roman Empire, Sack of Rome by the Visigoths
